subject: social_science
chapter_title: The Constitution of India, An Introduction

concepts.title: What Is a Constitution
concepts.definition: A constitution is the supreme rulebook of a state: it sets the structure of government, divides its powers, lists the rights of citizens and the duties of rulers, and stands above every ordinary law.
concepts.key_idea: A constitution is the game's rulebook for the nation: players and referees alike must play by it.

concepts.title: Making of the Indian Constitution
concepts.definition: India's Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly of elected and nominated members between 1946 and 1949; committees debated every clause, and it came into force on 26 January 1950.
concepts.key_idea: The Constitution was not decreed but deliberated: years of debate gave it the weight of a people's own choice.

concepts.title: The Preamble and Its Values
concepts.definition: The Preamble opens the Constitution by declaring India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic that secures justice, liberty, equality and fraternity for all its citizens.
concepts.formula: preamble = sovereign + socialist + secular + democratic + republic
concepts.key_idea: The Preamble is the Constitution in one breath: a summary of the nation's goals and promises.

concepts.title: The Constitution in Daily Life
concepts.definition: The Constitution touches daily life: it guarantees the rights you exercise at school and street, protects minorities, allows amendment by special procedure, and reminds every official that power is borrowed, not owned.
concepts.key_idea: The Constitution works when citizens use it: rights claimed and duties done keep it alive.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why is the constitution compared to a game's rulebook?

solution_template.explain: Every game needs agreed rules that even the strongest player must obey.
The constitution fixes how government is chosen and limited, so the strongest cannot rewrite play mid-game.
